content: This judgment addresses enforcement-related division proceedings involving jointly owned property in Civitavecchia, purchased in 1994 by two couples each owning half in legal community property. Following seizure by a creditor spouse against her debtor spouse's share in 2014, the enforcement judge ordered division proceedings instead of sale of the undivided share to avoid value reduction. The court rejected the inadmissibility objection for failure to undergo mandatory mediation, holding that Article 5(4)(e) of Legislative Decree 28/2010 excludes mediation in enforcement-related incidental proceedings. The court approved formation of three shares (25% creditor spouse, 25% enforcement proceedings, 50% other couple) as legal community between the spouses had dissolved pursuant to Article 191 of the Civil Code following their separation. The court rejected defendants' late counterclaim for adjustment of shares to account for management expenses as time-barred. Finding the property not conveniently divisible in kind based on court-appointed expert assessment showing division would cause depreciation, the court ordered dissolution through forced sale with proceeds allocated according to established shares. The property value was set at €200,000 with 20% reduction for absence of warranty in forced sales. Costs were imposed jointly and severally on defendants at €3,235.00 plus expenses.
